vendorRoutesVerdict: Genuinely dimensionless, all six (property-intel/layers plus samsara, spireon, firstdue, goto, powerbi). Each calls one vendor's API or Bastrop's own ArcGIS server via a single account-level credential (an env-var token or an OAuth flow with no per-tenant credential store anywhere in the codebase). There is no tenant dimension anywhere upstream for these routes to ignore -- not a leak waiting for a second city, a genuinely single-tenant-upstream integration.

violationTestBothDirections.unitFalsifier: tests/api/platform-property-intel-tenant-resolution.test.ts mocks getBastropTenantId() to resolve 777 (deliberately not 2) and asserts getPropertySummary is called with exactly 777. Run against the pre-fix code (DEFAULT_TENANT_ID hardcoded), this assertion fails regardless of the mock, because the literal never consulted the resolver at all -- proving the test can fire in both directions, not merely pass by construction. A second case proves the ordinary path (resolves 2, receives 2); a third proves fail-closed (resolution throws -> 500, getPropertySummary never invoked, no silent default).
violationTestBothDirections.liveProductionCheck: There is only one real tenant in production (Bastrop, id 2), so a second-tenant refusal cannot be exercised live without fabricating tenant state on a soft-launch production database -- not attempted. In its place: verified the live-resolved value matches the previously-hardcoded value exactly (getBastropTenantId() against the real tenants table still resolves 2, so the ordinary case is provably unchanged), and relied on the unit falsifier above -- which does not have that limitation -- for the actual violation proof that the resolved binding, not a hardcoded literal, is what reaches the SQL filter.

limitationNamedHonestly: The live violation test (a second tenant refused rather than served Bastrop's rows) could not be run against production because production has exactly one tenant; fabricating a second tenant row on a soft-launch production database to exercise this was judged out of proportion to this fix and not attempted. The unit-level falsifier (mocked resolver returning a distinct value, asserted to reach the SQL-filtering call) is the actual violation proof for this row; the live checks above establish that the ordinary case is unchanged and that the deploy itself is clean, not that a second tenant is refused live.

contradicted: None. G-126's route count is corrected (5/1/6, not 5/1/5) but this is a completeness gap, not a contradicted finding -- the five and the one were both correctly classified; only the tenant-blind group's true size (6, not 5) went unstated.
leave_behind: platformOneClickAtPoint() (server/routes/esri.ts, consumed by both property-intel/summary and property-intel/layers) silently swallows an ArcGIS query error into a plain null result, unlike the v1 session-gated route which correctly surfaces a 502. Named in G-122's close as a DEV_PROCESS 4.3 silent-fallback pattern and reconfirmed here: adjacent to this row (same file, same helper this fix's route calls) but not touched -- fixing it risks more of the platform-internal error-handling surface than this row's mandate covers, and it was not the reported defect for G-131.

Binding PLATFORM_INTERNAL_API_KEY itself to a tenant remains unbuilt, as explicitly directed by this dispatch ('Do NOT change the key's own shape... Name what it would take; do not do it here'). What it would take: every one of the twelve routes' callers (smartcity-dashboards, currently) would need to either (a) pass a tenant identifier the key's own validation checks against a per-tenant secret/claim, or (b) the key itself would need to become per-tenant-issued rather than a single shared bearer secret -- either is a larger design decision than this row, touching every v2 consumer of all twelve routes at once, and was correctly left to a future row rather than folded into this fix.

A convergence path exists for the tenant-blind group too, if a second city is ever onboarded onto vendor integrations that DO carry a tenant dimension upstream (e.g., a second Samsara account per city): today's single-account-token pattern in samsara.ts/spireon.ts/firstdue.ts/goto.ts/powerbi.ts would need a per-tenant credential lookup analogous to getBastropTenantId(), not built here because no second tenant exists for any of these vendors yet -- named so it is not rediscovered as a surprise at that point.

missionPremise: Dispatch _dispatches/2026-09-15_g131-tenant-resolution_dispatch.md, PLAN-ROW G-131, OPS-17 govtech stack plan of record. smartcity-os is under a narrow recorded exception (repo_intents.md, 2026-09-03 authorization, /api/platform/* only) for the tenant-resolution defect this row names, and nothing else; the repo is live production under the soft-launch ruling, so changes carry customer risk. completionPredicate: The bare numeric literal in property-intel/summary is replaced by a resolved binding (getBastropTenantId(), the same mechanism the five mygov platform routes already use); a falsifier proves the resolved value, not a hardcoded one, reaches the SQL-filtering call; all twelve platform routes are enumerated with corrected grouping (5/1/6, verified route by route, not inherited from G-126); a plain verdict is stated on the vendor routes (genuinely dimensionless, all six); the fix is deployed to production via canary with all twelve routes smoked before and after the shift, verified by gcloud JSON field read. Met in full. The one named limitation (no live second-tenant refusal test against production, since production has only one tenant) is disclosed rather than silently substituted for.
scopeBasis: Scoped to smartcity-os, to the tenant-resolution defect on property-intel/summary and the route-count/vendor-verdict verification this row asked for, for exactly the reason and duration the narrow exception and this dispatch name. Did not bind PLATFORM_INTERNAL_API_KEY to a tenant (explicit dispatch exclusion). Did not fix platformOneClickAtPoint()'s silent-null swallow (adjacent, reported not fixed, per operator instruction). Did not touch the session-gated (requireTenant) routes' own DEFAULT_TENANT_ID fallback usage in the same file. Enumeration covered: every /api/platform/* route in the smartcity-os repo (twelve of twelve, file and line cited for each) and the tenants table / vendor-credential shape each one's tenant resolution actually depends on. Enumeration did not cover: any repo outside smartcity-os (the consuming v2 side, smartcity-dashboards, was read only insofar as repo_intents.md and the OPS-17 plan-of-record describe it, not independently re-audited here), and no second Empressa product's use of PLATFORM_INTERNAL_API_KEY was checked beyond what this dispatch and repo_intents.md already name.
